_read_me: Tiers control how much weight the social layer gives an account - see sportsquant/social/extractor.py.
tier1_official and tier2_journalists: can set a 'confirmed' flag on a lineup/injury update.
tier3_community: analytics/aggregator accounts - useful context, but cross-check before treating as fact.
tier4_banter_and_unverified: entertainment, memes, rumours and parody accounts named in the project brief.
Never used as a factual signal, even indirectly - sentiment only, and only if you explicitly want it.
This list needs your own review: handles change hands, accounts get suspended, and 'is this account
actually satire' is a judgement call Claude did not verify one at a time. Treat it as a starting point.
Reading any of this requires your own X API bearer token in .env (X_BEARER_TOKEN) - see README.md
and docs/model_guide.tex section 8 for why that is not free, and roughly what it costs.

tier1_official.note: League and club verified accounts. Add the ones for the competitions you follow - handle per club/league.

tier2_journalists.note: Credentialed reporters with a track record of confirmed (not just claimed) lineup/transfer news.

tier3_community.note: Analytics, aggregator and fan-media accounts named in the project brief - good context, verify before treating as news.

tier4_banter_and_unverified.note: Named in the project brief as popular banter/rumour/parody accounts, including some the user identified as parody outright (e.g. Fabrizio Romano parody accounts). Sentiment/entertainment only - never a factual trigger, and never decoded or treated as a source of confirmed news.
